version.changelog: Docs: attribution signature updated to Pondsi (+MiMo-v2.5 +deepseek-v4.1-flash-expires-on-0910 +GLM5.3-flash) - automatically committed by OpenClaw. No functional change.

llm.summary: This skill makes a disclosed local OpenClaw UI modification and does not show evidence of hidden network access, credential access, or unrelated behavior.

dimensions.detail: Filesystem writes are limited to the OpenClaw Control UI dist directory and assets matching pcl-model-picker.v*.js, which is proportionate to the UI patch.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses PowerShell with ExecutionPolicy Bypass, auto-detects the OpenClaw Control UI directory, backs up index.html, copies one asset, and edits one script tag; no remote payload retrieval was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions encourage an agent to run the installer for install or repair requests; this is somewhat broad but aligned with the skill purpose and the modifying command is disclosed.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The injected script persists in index.html until uninstall or OpenClaw upgrade, but this persistence is clearly disclosed and reversible with -Remove.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to improve the OpenClaw Control UI model picker, and the bundled PowerShell installer plus browser JavaScript implement that UI-focused behavior.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm you want a local OpenClaw package patch and verify the detected Control UI path is correct. The skill is designed to edit index.html, copy a browser-side asset, and remove matching old picker assets; use the documented -Remove option to uninstall.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] expected: The broad activation concern is downgraded because the artifact frames command execution as an explicit install or repair action, and the target file changes are documented; users should still confirm the target path before allowing the patch.
